front.title: Congestion-Aware Reliability Enhancement Mechanism (CREM) for RDMA over IP Networks

abstract.t: RDMA transports designed for lossless data center fabrics perform poorly over long-distance, high bandwidth-delay product, or lossy IP paths: go-back-N retransmission resends whole windows, selective repeat costs at least a round trip per loss, and fixed forward erasure correction wastes capacity when the path is clean. This document specifies the Congestion-Aware Reliability Enhancement Mechanism (CREM), which protects datagram-based RDMA flows without modifying their packets. CREM adds a UDP-encapsulated repair channel on which the sender transmits erasure-coded repair symbols computed over blocks of RDMA packets, adapts the redundancy to measured loss and to whether losses are caused by congestion, and recovers losses that exceed the redundancy with a coded retransmission: a number of repair symbols, computed only over the lost packets, that is smaller than the number of lost packets. Per-packet retransmission remains as the final fallback. Optional path reports from on-path nodes, derived from Alternate Marking measurements or from the nodes' own drops, inform the adaptation.
